d001.note: p005 line 2: a small dagger alif is clearly printed over the final ى of «على» (zoom at 500 dpi). It is a visible printed mark, so it is kept as ىٰ per §2. The body font prints it on every final alef maqsura; the bold font does not (see «على الله» p006).

d002.note: p005 line 3: «وعلىٰ آله». The dagger alif over ى is clearly visible in the zoom, the same as d001.

d003.note: p005: «أخرىٰ،». The dagger alif over the final ى is clearly printed.

d004.note: p005: «علىٰ خير البرية». The dagger alif over ى is clearly printed.

d005.note: p005: «الحسنىٰ).». The dagger alif over the final ى is clearly printed at the start of the line.

d006.note: p006: «[الزمر:١٠]» (bold). I measured it at 600 dpi: the gap from the colon to ١ is 30 px and the gap between the digits ١ and ٠ is 38 px. So no space is printed after the colon, and A's spacing is kept.

d007.note: p006: «[آل عمران:٢٠٠]» (small, regular). The colon touches the digits (21 px gap against a 30 px gap between digits), so no space is printed.

d008.note: p006: «(رحمتك أرجىٰ عندي من عملي).». The dagger alif over the final ى is clearly printed in the regular font.

d009.note: p006: the print sets «مذهبنا:» on its own larger bold line. But CONVENTIONS §6 gives this exact text as its run-in label example («**مذهبنا:** حسن الظن…»), and STRUCTURE §3 also lists «مذهبنا:» and «طريقتنا:» as run-in labels, so A's run-in bold label follows the conventions. The statement after it is also printed bold, which A keeps as its own **…**.

d010.note: p006: «طريقتنا:» is the same case as d009. STRUCTURE §3 names it as a run-in bold label. The next line «ما وافق الشرع الشريف؛ إسلامًا، وإيمانًا، وإحسانًا.» is printed bold.

d011.note: p006: «عقيدتنا:» is treated like مذهبنا/طريقتنا (d009, d010) for consistency. The next line «الاعتماد على الله.» is printed bold, with no dagger alif on على in the bold font.

d012.note: p006: «[الأنعام:٩١]» is bold and the colon is set tight against ٩١ in the 900 dpi zoom, so no space is printed.

d013.note: p007 right caption: «السيد أبو الفيض» is a short centered line that is not stretched. The next line «أحمد ابن الصديق الغماري» is also centered, and the text from «ولد بطنجة…» onward is a kashida-justified block. Per §6 (a visibly short line ends a paragraph; centered short lines are their own paragraphs), each name line is its own paragraph.

d014.note: p007 right caption: «أحمد ابن الصديق الغماري» is a short centered line. A paragraph break follows it, before the justified «ولد بطنجة عام…» block (same reasoning as d013).

d015.note: p007 left caption: «السيد أبو الفضل» is a short centered line and its own paragraph, the same as d013.

d016.note: p007 left caption: «عبد الله ابن الصديق الغماري» is a short centered line. The justified «ولد بطنجة عام ١٣٢٨هـ…» block follows as its own paragraph (same as d014).
